transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Most nights after my wife goes to bed, I end up in the kitchen eating way more than a normal meal. Fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls—whatever leftovers are around. Sometimes I’ll eat until a whole tray, or half the fridge, is gone.
When these eating episodes happen, do you feel unable to stop or control how much you’re eating?

Yeah. Once I take that first bite, it feels like I’ve already decided, even if I’m telling myself to stop. I’ll think, “George, stop now,” but then I’m still fixing another plate or opening another container.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I’m not sure what you mean by that.
After you eat like that, have you ever made yourself throw up?
I… I don’t know. I haven’t really thought about it that way.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself throw up?
I’m honestly not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to what I do afterward in that way.
After you eat that way, do you ever make yourself vomit?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed myself doing that after eating.
After eating like that, do you ever take laxatives to try to get rid of the food?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself taking anything after eating like that.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can’t stop eating once you’ve started?
Yeah. Once I take that first bite, it feels like I’ve already decided, even if I’m telling myself to stop. I’ll keep making another plate or opening something else anyway.
After you eat that way, do you do anything to keep yourself from gaining weight?
I don’t think so. I mean, after I eat like that, I don’t usually do anything specific to try to keep from gaining weight.
How much does your body weight or shape affect how you feel about yourself?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t thought much about my weight or shape affecting how I feel about myself.
Do these eating episodes usually happen after you wake up from sleep during the night?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether it happens after I wake up at night.
Do these eating episodes upset you a lot?

Yeah, a lot. Afterward I feel sick with myself—ashamed and guilty, disgusted that I let it happen again. I’m supposed to be this organized, strong person, and then I’m sitting there feeling like a complete mess.
After you eat that way, do you ever fast the next day to make up for it?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I go without eating the next day because of it.
When this happens, do you eat an amount of food that most people would consider unusually large for one sitting?

Yes. Most nights after my wife goes to bed, I’ll get into the leftovers and eat way more than a normal meal—fried chicken, mac and cheese, sweet potatoes, rolls. Sometimes I keep going until a whole tray is gone, or half the fridge.
After these eating episodes, do you ever exercise hard on purpose to burn off the food?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I exercise hard afterward specifically because of eating like that.
When these episodes happen, have you usually just woken up from sleep?
I don’t really know. I haven’t noticed whether I’m waking up from sleep right before it happens.
After these episodes, do you ever do anything on purpose to get rid of the food you ate?
I’m not really sure what you mean by get rid of it. I haven’t paid attention to doing anything like that after.
When you start eating like that at night, are you fully awake?
I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m fully awake when it starts.
When these nighttime eating episodes happen, do you remember them clearly the next morning?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I remember them clearly the next morning.
After these eating episodes, do you ever do anything on purpose to make up for the eating, like getting rid of the food or trying to burn it off?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself doing anything afterward to make up for it.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation of recurrent episodes of eating an objectively large amount of food at night suggests a feeding/eating disorder. Added binge-eating disorder and bulimia nervosa as primary possibilities; retained unspecified eating disorder pending details about loss of control, compensatory behaviors, frequency, distress, and weight/shape concerns. Night eating syndrome/other specified feeding or eating disorder remains in the differential but is represented under other specified/unspecified categories in ICD-10-CM.
